column1: Project Title: Impact of Screen Time on Student Performance
Students with high screen time scored the highest average test score of 72.48. Low screen-time students scored 69.91, while medium screen-time students scored 69.26.
Students with high screen time spend an average of 1.64 hours on extracurricular activities. Low screen-time students spend 1.47 hours, while medium screen-time students spend 1.43 hours.
Students aged 13–15 achieved the highest average test score of 71.83. Students above 15 scored an average of 69.68.
The high screen-time group has the highest average test score.
Students aged 13–15 have higher average scores than students above 15.
The high screen-time group also reports slightly more extracurricular activity hours.
Students should maintain a balanced daily routine.
Students should give sufficient time to studies and extracurricular activities.
Screen time should be used productively for learning.
Academic performance should be monitored regularly.

This analysis compares screen time, test scores, age groups, and extracurricular activities. The results show differences in average academic performance across these groups. These comparisons do not establish that screen time or age directly causes changes in test scores.
